channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Cursor traces its tampered Claude Code extension to the Fireworks AI breach — up to 5,000 users may have installed it
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Two weeks after a malicious copy of Anthropic’s Claude Code extension turned up in its marketplace, Cursor has traced the intrusion to an access key exposed at inference vendor Fireworks AI — and says up to 5,000 developers may have installed the tampered build before it was pulled.

item.title: Design physical products with AI: hands-on with text-to-cad
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: text-to-cad (earthtojake/text-to-cad, 26,000+ GitHub stars, MIT) turns your coding agent into a CAD engineer: it writes build123d Python, a local server builds it, and the same pipeline checks whether a shop can actually make the part. This tutorial installs it, connects an agent, and builds a parametric phone stand from prompt to printable STL.

item.title: Claude wrote a language model for DOS that fits on a floppy disk — and the thread caught a terms problem
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: A Reddit poster says Fable 5.2 wrote a 367,000-parameter transformer that runs under DOS, with Opus 5.5 generating its training data — program and weights together about 435 KB. The 71-second demo charmed r/ClaudeAI, then the comments turned to Anthropic's terms.

item.title: Salesforce's SOV-Transcribe-1 takes the open-weights speech crown at 2.3% word error
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Salesforce has released SOV-Transcribe-1, an open-weights speech model that leads every other downloadable transcriber on the Artificial Analysis benchmark — but at 53 GB of weights and no live streaming, it is built for recorded audio and self-hosted use, not real-time captions.

item.title: SpaceX cuts about 60 from Grok Imagine's team as its AI bet shifts to coding tools and Grok Bot
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The Information reports SpaceX's AI group laid off roughly 60 people from the team behind Grok Imagine, leaving a handful to keep the image and video generator running — the latest cut in a unit that has been thinning since xAI folded into SpaceX.

item.title: OpenAI closes its standalone robotics team and hands the job to GPT-6 Astra
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Fortune reports OpenAI has folded its standalone robotics team into its main research and applied groups, arguing that general-purpose models like GPT-6 Astra can now drive robots directly — a bet that robotics is no longer a special problem.

item.title: Fable 5.2 painted a Bob Ross landscape in a browser Paint clone — and Reddit crowned it ‘Claude Ross’
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Fable 5.2 spent 94 minutes and 11,066 brush strokes painting a sunset landscape — pine trees, a lake, mountains — in a browser clone of MS Paint. Reddit’s verdict: ‘Claude Ross.’

item.title: Antigravity Dynamic Workflows: run a team of coding agents from one reviewable Python script
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google's Antigravity shipped Dynamic Workflows on November 13: type /run-workflow and the agent writes a short Python script that fans your task out across parallel subagents, collects schema-validated results, and hands you a summary. This tutorial runs three workflows end to end — and shows when to use them instead of a swarm.

item.title: ai-memory: one memory for every coding agent — hands-on with cross-agent handoffs
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: ai-memory (akitaonrails/ai-memory, MIT) gives every coding agent one shared memory: a local server, a git-backed markdown wiki, and typed handoffs that let you quit Claude Code mid-task and resume in Codex without re-explaining anything. This guide installs v3.4.6, verifies the server, the search, and a real handoff — no API key required.

item.title: Pinky: let your AI agent use your phone — hands-on with the MCP bridge for iPhone and Android
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Pinky 2026.1115.4 is the open-source MCP server that lets Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor operate a real iPhone or Android — with you approving the risky steps. This guide installs it, verifies its checksum, runs the full agent loop against the demo phones, and wires up a real agent and a real phone — every verified step run in a sandbox.

item.title: Google's Antigravity agent teams formalize the Weil conjectures and prove a 2013 open problem
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google’s /teamwork multi-agent system, running on Gemini 4, formalized the Weil conjectures in 1.8 million lines of Lean, helped settle a 2013 information-theory conjecture, and rewrote a video decoder in Rust — faster than the original. Not all of it can be independently checked yet.

item.title: Sierra releases Poppy 1.0: a standard for personal AI agents, live on every Shopify store and checked first by Meta’s Muse
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Sierra’s Personal Agent Protocol reaches 1.0: every Shopify store now publishes a Poppy file automatically, Meta’s Muse looks for one on every site it visits, and more than 100 companies have signed on as design partners.

item.title: Stop asking your LLM to decide: Perplexity Decider v1.3 hands-on
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Perplexity Decider v1.3 returns probabilities instead of prose: route tickets, score severity, and extract spans with three typed questions — locally via Ollama or on the hosted Decisions API. Every command verified, including the MLX gotcha that blocks Flash on Linux.

item.title: Hands-on with SolidCraft: open-source parametric CAD your AI agent can drive
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: SolidCraft 0.42.0 is the open-source parametric CAD app your AI agent can drive: 647 commands, a 22-tool MCP server, and a JSON script format that builds real parts. This guide installs it, builds a bracket, changes its parameters, hands it to an agent over MCP, and renders it — every step verified.

item.title: OpenCode: the open-source AI coding agent that works with any model — hands-on
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenCode passed 226,000 GitHub stars the week its 2.3.0 release shipped: a terminal coding agent that runs free models with no account, local Ollama models, or any paid provider. Install it, run a real task, and wire up a local model — every command verified.

item.title: IBM’s Nighthawk r3 targets 520 qubits — and a 1,040-qubit machine in 2027
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: IBM’s next quantum processor is designed to run 10,000 operations across 520 qubits, and two of them linked together would pass 1,000 qubits in 2027 — but the chip is still a design target, and the numbers that matter today come from its predecessor.

item.title: Plannotator: stay in the loop with your coding agents — hands-on with the review workspace for plans, diffs, and feedback
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Plannotator is the No. 1 trending repo on GitHub today: a local review surface where you annotate your coding agent's plans, review its diffs, and send feedback back as its next turn. Install the 0.28.64 binary, review a real diff, annotate a document, and open the Inbox — no API key, no account, everything on localhost.

item.title: “AI video has come pretty far”: the 86-second UFO trailer Reddit can’t stop rewatching
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A 1:26 montage by creator tupacabra stitches Tesla, Nazi troops, starships and a 1915 recording of Kipling’s “Boots” into a UFO-lore trailer — and r/singularity’s verdict is split between awe and “still just a trailer.”

item.title: Meta lets Muse make your phone calls: outbound calling opens to paid US subscribers
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Meta’s Muse assistant can now ring US businesses on your behalf — restaurants, insurers, the DMV — but only for paying subscribers. The feature, tested since September, went wide on November 12.

item.title: Stop copy-pasting SKILL.md files: install any agent skill with one command
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Vercel's skills CLI installs any agent skill from GitHub into every coding agent you use, with a lock file and an update check. Every command verified — no account, no API key.

item.title: Fable 5.2 built a swimmable underwater world in a single 97 KB HTML file — and Reddit is diving in
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A Reddit user turned one Claude Code prompt into Abyssal Garden — a swimmable, fully procedural underwater world that ships as a single 96.8 KB HTML file. It took off on r/ClaudeAI within hours.

item.title: LoopForge Local: Turn Claude Code Into a Staged Delivery Pipeline
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Tencent’s LoopForge hit GitHub trending this week. Its Local edition installs a staged, human-gated delivery workflow into Claude Code with one npx command — no server, no Docker. Every step verified.

item.title: Google’s Gemini glasses are real: pre-orders open at $395, in stores December 10
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Google and Samsung opened pre-orders for Gemini-powered Intelligent Eyewear on November 12 — Warby Parker frames from $395, Gentle Monster from $449 — with a December 10 launch in the US and South Korea, and a privacy pitch aimed at the bystanders as much as the wearers.

item.title: Put your agent in a real UI: hands-on with AG-UI, the protocol that connects agents to frontends
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: AG-UI is the open protocol that turns any agent into a streaming, tool-calling, state-sharing UI — the missing third leg next to MCP and A2A. Build a working server in Python, drive it from TypeScript, and add a real tool call. Every command verified, no API key needed for the core loop.

item.title: Build a streaming AI chat app with the Vercel AI SDK and a local Ollama model — no API key needed
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: A complete streaming chatbot — Next.js, AI SDK 7, and a local Ollama model — with a working tool call and zero API keys. Every command verified end to end.
